conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Aestivation (Arrangement of Floral Parts in Bud)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Aestivation (Arrangement of Floral Parts in Bud)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Vexillary aestivation has 1 posterior Standard, 2 lateral Wings, and 2 anterior fused Keel petals (Fabaceae). Parietal placentation in Mustard has a false septum (Replum).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
AESTIVATION PATTERNS
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
  VALVATE                         TWISTED                         IMBRICATE
Margins touch without           One margin overlaps next        Margins overlap irregularly
overlapping.                     regularly in one direction.     without definite direction.
└── *Calotropis*                 └── *China rose*, *Cotton*      └── *Cassia*, *Gulmohar*
conceptBreakdown.content:
Aestivation is the mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl.

• **Valvate**: Sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin without overlapping (*Calotropis*).
• **Twisted**: One margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one regularly in one direction (*China rose*, *Lady's finger*, *Cotton*).
• **Imbricate**: Margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction (*Cassia*, *Gulmohar*).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VEXILLARY / PAPILIONACEOUS AESTIVATION
                     
   [ Standard / Vexillum ] (1 Large Posterior Outer)
              │
   [ Wings / Alae ] (2 Lateral Free)
              │
   [ Keel / Carina ] (2 Smallest Anterior Fused)
conceptBreakdown.content: Characteristic of family **Fabaceae** (Pea, Bean). In a flower with five petals, the largest posterior petal (**Standard / Vexillum**) overlaps the two lateral petals (**Wings / Alae**), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals fused together to form a boat-shaped structure (**Keel / Carina**). Formula: $1 + 2 + (2)$.

conceptBreakdown.title: 5.3 Placentation Architectures
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PLACENTATION ARCHITECTURES
                           
  MARGINAL                AXILE                   PARIETAL
  Placenta along ventral  Placenta axial in       Ovules on inner wall
  suture of monocarpellary multilocular ovary.    of unilocular ovary.
  ovary.                  └── *China rose*,       └── *Mustard*, *Argemone*
  └── *Pea*                   *Tomato*, *Lemon*       (False septum: **Replum**)
  
  FREE-CENTRAL            BASAL                   SUPERFICIAL
  Ovules on central axis; Placenta at base;       Ovules on inner walls

  └── *Dianthus*,         └── *Sunflower*,        └── *Nymphaea* (Water Lily)

conceptBreakdown.content:
Placentation refers to the arrangement of ovules within the ovary cavity:

1. **Marginal**: The placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of a monocarpellary unilocular ovary, and ovules are borne in two alternating rows (*Pea*).
2. **Axile**: Placenta is axial in a multicarpellary syncarpous multilocular ovary, with ovules attached in each locule (*China rose*, *Tomato*, *Lemon*).
3. **Parietal**: Ovules develop on the inner wall of the unilocular ovary or on peripheral outgrowths. Ovary becomes 2-locular due to formation of a false septum called the **Replum** (*Mustard*, *Argemone*).
4. **Free-Central**: Ovules are borne on a central axis, and septa are completely absent (*Dianthus*, *Primrose*).
5. **Basal**: Placenta develops at the base of the ovary and bears a single ovule (*Sunflower*, *Marigold*).
6. **Superficial**: Ovules develop all around the inner surfaces of partition walls in a multilocular ovary (*Nymphaea* - Water Lily).
